message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find the Full Text | |-------|------------|-----------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • 55 mph on rural interstates
• 65 mph on urban interstates (unless posted otherwise)
• 45 mph on rural highways, 35 mph on urban highways (unless posted)
• 25 mph in school zones during school hours | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001–545.004 | | **Seat‑Belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts (Sec. 545.001).
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster (Sec. 545.001).
• No “seat‑belt law” for rear‑seat adults, but rear‑seat seat‑belt use is encouraged. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.001 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal for drivers over 21 (Sec. 545.021).
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 % is illegal).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (Sec. 545.021).
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks (Sec. 545.021).
• Stop at stop signs and yield at yield signs (Sec. 545.021).
• “Left‑turn on red” is allowed after a full stop unless sign prohibits it (Sec. 545.021). | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights (Sec. 545.021).
• Vehicles must stop on both sides of the road if the bus is in a two‑lane road. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots (Sec. 545.021).
• No “passing on the right” unless the vehicle ahead is turning left (Sec. 545.021). | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of a driveway, fire hydrant, or on a sidewalk (Sec. 545.021).
• Parking in a “no parking” zone is a violation (Sec. 545.021). | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate (Sec. 545.021).
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection (Sec. 545.021). | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches (Sec. 545.021). | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing of a vehicle requires a tow‑away permit (Sec. 545.021). | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | --- ### How to Access the Full Texas Transportation Code 1. **Texas Legislature Online** – The official source for all statutes: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ Navigate to Title 7 (Transportation) → Chapter 545 (Traffic Rules). 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Provides driver handbooks and quick‑reference guides: https://www.txdmv.gov/ 3. **Legal Information Websites** – e.g., FindLaw, Nolo, or Cornell’s Legal Information Institute offer searchable versions of the Texas statutes. --- ### Quick Tips for Texas Drivers - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they can vary by county and even within a city. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. - **Check your mirrors** before changing lanes; Texas law requires a “proper look” before overtaking. - **Keep your vehicle’s registration and inspection stickers up to date** to avoid fines. - **Know the school bus rules** – stopping for a bus is mandatory, regardless of the direction of travel. --- #### Need More Specific Information? If you’re looking for details on a particular aspect (e.g., “What are the penalties for a 0.09 % BAC?” or “How does Texas handle “right‑of‑way” at a four‑way stop?”), let me know and I can pull up the exact statutory language or provide a deeper dive.
